summary: Clinton County, PA steel tower built 1923 and removed 1990 (early 1990s per a 2012 caption); a 2012 caption says the cabin sits at the site and the tower foundation remains; a PA Environment Digest item of unconfirmed date says the cabin serves as The Nature Conservancy Lodge.

facts.design: Steel tower about 60 feet tall on four legs, supporting a square metal cabin (Forest Lookouts quotes an NGS description); Blaw-Knox steel per the register
facts.status_note: Tower removed (1990 per the register). A 2012 caption says the cabin sits at the site and the tower foundation remains. A PA Environment Digest item of unconfirmed date says the cabin serves as The Nature Conservancy Lodge. No source says whether the public can visit or rent the lodge.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the 1926 article date the steel tower to 1923, but an October 1920 report describes a fire observation tower on the same ridge. The sources do not say whether an earlier structure stood there. The story presents this as an open question.
The register gives 1,987 ft (606 m), matching the brief's 605.6 m. The 1926 article gives a ground elevation of about 2,240 feet. The story gives no elevation.

notes_for_editor: Built date (1923) and the October 1920 fire-tower report on the same ridge do not match; the story says so and does not settle it. The Lock Haven Express material is quoted second-hand from the Forest Lookouts page, not checked against the newspaper. The cabin is reported as a Nature Conservancy lodge in a Nature Conservancy preserve (2012 caption; newsletter item of unconfirmed date); no source says whether visitors or renters may enter, so check with the owner before publishing directions. The 1926 route description (from Renovo via Hyner) is historical and should not be printed as current directions. The photo (CC BY 2.0, Nicholas A. Tonelli, 2012) is a new find.
